what: World definitions gain a JSON form, read by the same rules, and a JSON Schema derived from those rules that each file names in $schema, so an editor validates the file as written; the TOML form is removed and a test keeps it removed.
why: rudy wants no TOML in strata's world (#20: "I dont want any toml..no. json"); TOML is a reverie carry-over, NPC definitions are about to grow nested data, and a derived JSON Schema lets an editor validate a world file as it is written.

criteria.then: offerWindowTicks, the values in authored order, the five importance words, every room, every item and every person's id, name, location, ties, places and values equal a hand-written literal of what the TOML files held
criteria.atBase: Base loads the TOML files into these same definitions; the test passes at base and must keep passing over the JSON files at head.

criteria.given: world/ and tests/worlds/two-tick as committed, and a copy of world/ whose people/mux.json sets values_draft to the string "yes"
criteria.then: the rogue, glitch and mux definitions carry values_draft true, no two-tick person carries values_draft, and the copy refuses naming people/mux.json, path values_draft and rule invalid_type
criteria.atBase: Base personSchema has no values_draft, so the loaded definitions lack it and the copy (JSON files only) refuses with missing-file for world.toml; the test fails at base.

criteria.given: a copy of world/ whose files carry $schema and $comment at their root, and a second copy whose rooms/back-room.json adds a root key extra
criteria.then: the first loads with no definition carrying a $schema or $comment key, and the second refuses naming rooms/back-room.json, an empty path and rule unrecognized_keys
criteria.atBase: Base reads world.toml, which the JSON copy lacks, so both loads refuse with missing-file; the test fails at base.

criteria.given: a copy of world/ whose items/stimpak.json is cut off mid-object
criteria.then: boot refuses naming items/stimpak.json, an empty path and rule json-syntax, and no database file is created
criteria.atBase: Base reads world.toml, which the copy lacks, so it refuses with missing-file and rule missing-file, not json-syntax; the test fails at base.

criteria.given: each refusal case the TOML tests broke today (boot C2's five, values V2's eight, knowledge's place case, server's two reset cases), applied as a JSON edit or removal of the same field in a copy of world/
criteria.when: the engine boots or the server resets on it
criteria.then: each refuses with the path and rule it refused with under TOML, naming the same file with .json in place of .toml, and no database is created
criteria.atBase: Base reads world.toml, which the JSON copies lack, so every case refuses with missing-file for world.toml; the tests fail at base.

criteria.given: the committed schemas/world.schema.json, values.schema.json, room.schema.json, person.schema.json and item.schema.json
criteria.when: each is parsed and compared with worldJsonSchemas() for its kind
criteria.then: each equals it, and a rule or description change in definitions.ts without rerunning bun run schemas makes the comparison differ
criteria.atBase: Base exports no worldJsonSchemas and no schemas/ file exists; the test fails at base.

criteria.when: write-schemas runs with that directory as its output
criteria.then: it holds exactly world.schema.json, values.schema.json, room.schema.json, person.schema.json and item.schema.json, each parsing equal to worldJsonSchemas() for its kind
criteria.atBase: Base has no write-schemas command; the test fails at base.

criteria.given: the JSON files under world/ and tests/worlds/two-tick
criteria.when: each file's $schema is resolved relative to the file
criteria.then: all 18 files exist (world.json, values.json, each room, person and item) and each names the committed schema of its kind: world.json the world schema, values.json the values schema, rooms/ the room schema, people/ the person schema, items/ the item schema
criteria.atBase: Base holds no JSON world file, so the 18 expected files are missing; the test fails at base.

criteria.when: every file under them is listed recursively
criteria.atBase: Base holds 18 .toml world files; the test fails at base.

criteria.when: the world, values and person schemas are read
criteria.then: rules.offer_window_ticks's description says ticks an offer stays open before it lapses unanswered, the values importance description and the person values description each say every value is rated with an integer from 0 to 4 read by the importance words, and the person values_draft description says the importances are a draft
criteria.atBase: Base schemas carry no descriptions and base exports no worldJsonSchemas; the test fails at base.

criteria.given: world/values.json, tests/worlds/two-tick/values.json and world/people/rogue.json, glitch.json and mux.json
criteria.then: both values.json carry a $comment citing Schwartz (2012), An Overview of the Schwartz Theory of Basic Values, and each of the three person files carries a $comment saying the importances were drafted by the assistant, experiment-grade, rudy 2026-11-10, derived from this world's ties
criteria.atBase: Base holds no JSON world file; the test fails at base.

criteria.when: each import specifier naming a path under world/ is resolved from its file
criteria.then: every one resolves to an existing file
criteria.atBase: Base's 16 imports name world/values.toml, which exists at base; the test passes there and fails at head unless each import moves with the file.

criteria.then: the world/ row says the definitions are JSON, a schemas/ row says it holds the JSON Schemas derived from the loader's rules, and no line names TOML world definitions
criteria.atBase: Base README says world/ holds the definitions in TOML and has no schemas/ row; the test fails at base.

criteria.then: it names world/values.json and world.json where it named world/values.toml and world.toml, and names no .toml world file
criteria.atBase: Base parked.md names world/values.toml and world.toml; the test fails at base.

criteria.then: it is still TOML and pins the install linker to hoisted
criteria.atBase: Base bunfig.toml is TOML with linker hoisted; the test passes at base and must keep passing.

outOfScope.summary: A JSON world file with a duplicate key loads with the last value, where TOML refused it; biome's noDuplicateObjectKeys refuses it in every committed world, so only a world kept outside the repository and loaded by --world goes unchecked.

frequency.command: docs/work/world-json/shape/evidence/frequencies.txt: git grep of --world, worldDir and WORLD over src, tests and harness/src
frequency.records: every world directory strata's code and tests load

outOfScope.summary: No test runs the committed JSON Schema as a validator over the world files: no JSON Schema validator is a dependency, so acceptance rests on the schema equalling zod's derivation of the rules that accept every file, and on the operator's editor walk.

frequency.reason: It is a check left to derivation and the operator's editor walk, not a usage path: every committed world file is loaded by the zod rules the schema is derived from, and the drift test holds the schema equal to that derivation.

outOfScope.summary: The JSON Schema carries shape rules only: the seven cross-reference rules (exit to names a room, location, tie target, place, value names the catalogue, every value rated, holder) are not expressible in it, so an editor does not flag them and boot still refuses them.

frequency.records: every named refusal rule in the loader

outOfScope.summary: unique-id (an id defined in two files of one kind) and unique-value-id (a value id repeated in values.json) are not expressible in a per-file JSON Schema either, so an editor does not flag them and boot still refuses them.

frequency.records: every named refusal rule in the loader

outOfScope.summary: Dated records keep the .toml paths they recorded: corpus preregistrations, briefs and comments, closed docs/work design and work-order files, and the closed npc-knowledge and npc-relationships explorations (strata-d3's ruling).

frequency.command: docs/work/world-json/shape/evidence/toml-records.txt: git grep -n .toml over corpus non-.ts files and corpus .ts non-import lines; git grep -l -i toml over docs/work and docs/explorations
frequency.records: 48 corpus prose lines and 13 docs files naming TOML, less parked.md which moves

walks.when: after merge, the operator opens world/people/mux.json in VS Code, sets values.power to 5, then hovers rules.offer_window_ticks in world/world.json
walks.then: the editor marks power as above the maximum of 4, and the hover shows that ticks are how long an offer stays open before it lapses unanswered
walks.operatorOnly: An editor's live schema diagnostics and hover text render only in the operator's editor window; no session, worker or command can see what the editor shows.

stakes: One source of rules: the zod schemas in src/engine/definitions.ts check the JSON and generate the JSON Schema; the committed schema is a derived artifact, held equal to its source by a test.
Every refusal the TOML loader named still refuses with the same path and rule, the file named .json; a JSON syntax error refuses as json-syntax with an empty path.
The loaded definitions are what they were: $schema and $comment are dropped at the loader and reach no def, snapshot or reader; values_draft is the only added field, typed, by strata-d3's ruling.
No TOML comment's meaning is dropped: field explanations become schema descriptions an editor shows; provenance becomes $comment; the draft mark becomes the typed values_draft.
No TOML file remains under world/ or tests/worlds/, and a test fails when one appears; bunfig.toml stays TOML.
Every runnable world reader, including the 16 corpus scripts, reads .json; dated records keep the paths they recorded.
